key_insight: Train a Code LLM and a Test LLM adversarially via reinforcement learning so tests and solutions co-evolve, producing dynamic, verifiable rewards that scale with model ability and avoid trivial self-collusion.
problem_solved: Addresses scarcity and stagnation of high-quality unit tests for RL-based code generation and the self-play dilemma where a single model either cheats (white-box) or generates generic, weak tests (black-box).
method: Maintain two distinct models — a Code LLM that writes solutions and a Test LLM that generates unit tests — and train them in an adversarial RL loop so each continuously challenges the other.
Use verifiable, executable pass/fail rewards from generated tests as the RL signal, while applying constraints and diversity incentives on the Test LLM to prevent trivial or collusive tests.
Periodically evaluate with held-out benchmarks and update policies to ensure test difficulty grows with capability and to preserve generalization beyond model-specific idiosyncrasies.
impact: Creates a scalable, self-improving reward pipeline for code generation that reduces dependence on handcrafted test suites and yields more robust, generalizable code models — useful for researchers and engineers improving code LLM reliability.
